output.brief:
Don't send the breach notice. The rise is not mainly a handling problem. Pelion, handled by the same Tessaly crew pool, stayed flat at about 3.7. For Corvane, the whole increase is in bags sent to the manual encode desk. Those bags went from 70 a day to about 460 a day. Their encode wait went from 7 to 33 minutes, and 91% of the failures reached the make-up lateral after it closed. Auto-read bags are unchanged.

The trigger is the 1 Sep switch to Fennick tag stock. Corvane tags printed with it fail automatic reading 11.8% of the time, against 1.5% on Brackwater. On 14–16 Oct, Brackwater tags at counters failed 1.6% while kiosk tags printed the same days on Fennick failed 12.1%. Transfer tags and Pelion tags were unaffected, which rules out the airport's readers.

What I can't tell yet is whether the Fennick stock is itself defective or whether the printer heat settings don't suit it. Don't lodge a defect claim yet.

Next steps:
1. Return to Brackwater stock now. About five weeks are in stores, and the switch is reversible.
2. Test Fennick separately, including the printer settings.
3. Ask HBAA about extra encode capacity as a temporary measure.
4. Hold the fee decision until the rate falls.

I'm fairly confident (about 85%).
